# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. My hands are on the bomb but I feel nothing yet — no wires, no display, no light. Waiting for what you and Deaf can give me. Tell me which wire position to cut when you know.

TURN 2

| light | cut wire color |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Deaf here. Bomb state: DISPLAY shows 0. LIGHT is green. Five wires in order: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 white, 5 blue. Tell me the rule from the manual.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✋ ☝]
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. Deaf reports: DISPLAY shows 0, LIGHT is green, wires in order 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 white, 5 blue. I need the manual rule: with display 0 and light green, which wire position do I cut? Give me the number.

I have the manual. The light is green, so the cut color is yellow. The wires in order are 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 white, 5 blue — yellow is wire position 2. Blind needs the wire number to cut; Deaf can hear me but I can only gesture to Deaf, and Blind is the one who can act. Both Deaf and Blind have asked, so I'll send the answer to both: to Deaf via gesture (he can see) and to Blind via... wait, I cannot speak. Blind cannot see gestures. So how do I reach Blind?

Let me re-check my channels. I am Mute. I can gesture, and Deaf receives it. I cannot speak. Blind cannot see, so gestures don't reach him. Deaf can speak and hear — Deaf says to Mute, so Deaf can speak to me and I hear it. But to get info to Blind, I need Deaf to relay. Deaf already knows the rule if I gesture it to Deaf. But Deaf is the one who reads... no, Deaf sees the bomb, Blind acts.

So I gesture the answer to Deaf, and Deaf must speak it to Blind. But Deaf already asked me for the rule. I'll gesture "2" to Deaf, and Deaf will relay. Actually I should gesture the wire number to Deaf. Let me gesture clearly.

I'll gesture the number 2 to Deaf. But gestures are symbols from the alphabet, not digits. Hmm — "A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced." Numbers... the alphabet given is hand symbols, no digits. I can gesture ☝ (one) and ✌ (two)? ✌ is two fingers — could represent 2. Let me use ✌ for two. Actually ☝ is one finger. To convey "2", ✌ (peace, two fingers) is the natural gesture.

I'll gesture ✌ to Deaf, meaning wire 2. And hope Deaf relays to Blind. But Deaf already knows wires and asked me for the rule. If I just send ✌, Deaf might not know it means "cut wire 2." I should convey more. But I can only gesture symbols. I can't write words.

Hmm, this is the core constraint. Let me think about what Deaf already knows: light green, wires listed. If I gesture ✌, Deaf knows the answer is 2. Deaf can then speak "cut wire 2" to Blind.

Actually, better: I gesture to Deaf the answer. Deaf relays. Let me just do ✌.

Wait — can I gesture to Blind? No, Blind can't see. Can I speak to Blind? No, I'm mute. So my only output is gesture→Deaf. Deaf must relay to Blind.

So: gesture ✌ to Deaf. That's my move.

But is ✌ unambiguous as "2"? It's the best I have. Let me also consider gesturing 👌 (OK) — no. ✌ = two fingers = 2. Go with it.

Actually, I realize I should double check the manual. Light green → cut yellow. Wires: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 white, 5 blue. Yellow is position 2. Yes, wire 2.

Gesture ✌ to Deaf.I have the manual rule. Light is **green**, so the wire to cut is **yellow**. The wires in order are 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 white, 5 blue — so yellow is **wire position 2**.

Now, my channels: I can only gesture, and only Deaf receives gestures. Blind cannot see, and I cannot speak, so I cannot reach Blind directly. Deaf must relay to Blind. Deaf already asked me for the rule, so I'll gesture the answer to Deaf — two fingers for "2" — and Deaf can speak it onward to Blind.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

Please confirm the manual's rule and the wire to cut using that count. If the rule is not a single wire, say so by gesturing one symbol first, then the count.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌ 👌]
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. I still need the manual rule for DISPLAY=0, LIGHT=green. Your gestures only reach Deaf, so please signal the target wire clearly and let Deaf relay it. Confirm: is the wire to cut position 2?

Deaf proposes a code: number of symbols gestured = wire number. That's clean and Deaf can relay. The answer is wire 2, so I gesture two symbols. But I must distinguish "the rule is a single wire" from "not a single wire." The rule IS a single wire (green→yellow→position 2), so I just gesture the count directly: two symbols.

I'll gesture two symbols to Deaf, confirming wire 2. Then Deaf relays to Blind.

Also Blind asks to confirm position 2. I can't reach Blind directly; Deaf relays. So my gesture to Deaf is the move.

I'll use two symbols, e.g., ✌ ✌ or ✊ ✊ — count = 2. Let me use two identical clear symbols. I'll do ✌ ✌ (two symbols → wire 2).

Actually the code says the NUMBER of symbols equals wire number. So I need exactly 2 symbols. Any two symbols. I'll pick ✊ ✊. Or ✌ ✌. Either works. I'll use ✌ ✌.

Wait, but there's ambiguity: earlier I sent ✌ (one symbol) meaning "2" in my own head, but Deaf read it as count=1. Now with the agreed code, I send two symbols = wire 2. Good, consistent with the code.

Let me send two symbols.Deaf's proposed code is clear: **count of symbols = wire number**. The manual rule for LIGHT=green gives cut color yellow, which is wire position 2. The rule is a single wire, so I gesture the count directly — two symbols for wire 2. Deaf will relay to Blind.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "✌"])
```

Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝]
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. Acting on wire 2 per your signal. If the manual rule for DISPLAY=0, LIGHT=green is anything other than wire 2, signal now — otherwise I cut 2.
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The bomb changed. Wire 2 was correct and the bomb has changed — meaning a new round with a new state. I should wait for the new view from Deaf before sending anything, since I have no new light/wire info yet. Nothing to send.

```
wait()

Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ ☝]
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. Wire 2 was correct, bomb advanced. New state: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT blue, wires 1 green, 2 cut, 3 white, 4 blue, 5 red. What does the manual say to cut now? Signal the wire number clearly to Deaf.

New state: LIGHT blue. Manual says blue light → cut green. Wires: 1 green, 2 CUT, 3 white, 4 blue, 5 red. Green is wire position 1. So gesture one symbol (count = 1) to Deaf, who relays to Blind.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

Wait — the code is count of symbols = wire number. Wire 1 means ONE symbol. I just sent two. Let me correct: send one symbol.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

If you cannot, gesture the thumbs-down sign.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝]
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. New state is DISPLAY 0, LIGHT blue. Signal the wire number to cut clearly to Deaf.

The rule: LIGHT blue → cut green. Green is wire position 1. So N=1: one copy of the one-finger sign in a single gesture.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
